question: Estimate Tier-3 city/town adoption of paid OTT subscriptions over next 3 years.
idealClarificationQuestions: Tier 3 cities + small towns (~5,000 with population 50K-500K, total ~240M people)? Yes.
Paid OTT (any single subscription, including JioCinema after monetization)? Yes.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Frame the approach
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Bottom-up: smartphone-enabled households → smart TV / streaming-stick adoption → willingness to pay.

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Households with at least one smart TV / Firestick / streaming device: ~10M (today, growing).

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Drivers for next 3 years: smart TV affordability (₹15K Mi/Realme), Jio/Airtel telco bundles, vernacular content (Mahabharat, regional cinema OTT).

expectedLogicalStructure.label: Calculate
expectedLogicalStructure.description: Projected 2029: ~28-32% of Tier 3 HH paying for at least one OTT = ~16-18M HH.

benchmarkAssumptions.parameter: Households with broadband or 4G/5G phone capable
Households with at least one smart TV / Firestick / streaming device
Currently paying for any OTT (mostly mobile-only ₹49 packs)

benchmarkAssumptions.value: smart TV affordability (₹15K Mi/Realme), Jio/Airtel telco bundles, vernacular content (Mahabharat, regional cinema OTT).
~28-32% of Tier 3 HH paying for at least one OTT = ~16-18M HH.

calculationFlow: Currently paying for any OTT (mostly mobile-only ₹49 packs): ~6-7M = 12-13% of HH.
Drivers for next 3 years: smart TV affordability (₹15K Mi/Realme), Jio/Airtel telco bundles, vernacular content (Mahabharat, regional cinema OTT).
Projected 2029: ~28-32% of Tier 3 HH paying for at least one OTT = ~16-18M HH.

finalAnswerRange.ideal: Projected 2029: ~28-32% of Tier 3 HH paying for at least one OTT = ~16-18M HH.
